s: Mahâvîra has explored all beings (whether moving or not, on high, below, and on earth)
q: This wise man had explored all beings, whether they move or not, on high, below, and on earth, as well as the eternal and transient things.

s: Karman is annihilated by Mahâvîra (all his Karman)
q: Having annihilated all his Karman, the great sage by his knowledge, virtue, and faith reached the insurpassable, highest perfection, a state which has a beginning but no end.

s: Nirvâna is chief object of the Law
q: as Nirvâna is the chief object of the Law,

s: Nirvâna is taught by Mahâvîra (as the best teacher among those who have taught it)
q: so is Gñâtriputra the best of those who have taught the Nirvâna.

s: Samsâra is crossed by Mahâvîra (as a flood)
q: Omniscient, wandering about without a home, crossing the flood (of the Samsâra), wise, and of an unlimited perception, without an equal, he shines forth (or he does penance) like the sun,

s: contemplation is practised by Mahâvîra (highest and purest of pure)
q: After having taught the highest Law he practised the highest contemplation, which is the purest of pure, pure without a flaw, thoroughly white (as it were) like mother-of-pearl and the moon.

s: austerities are practised by Mahâvîra (for the removal of pain)
q: he practised austerities for the removal of pain,

s: Mahâvîra has explored eternal and transient things
q: This wise man had explored all beings, whether they move or not, on high, below, and on earth, as well as the eternal and transient things.

s: Kriyâvâdins have doctrines doctrines
q: He understood the doctrines of the Kriyâvâdins, of the Akriyâvâdins, of the Vainayikas, and of the Agñânavâdins;

s: Akriyâvâdins have doctrines doctrines
q: He understood the doctrines of the Kriyâvâdins, of the Akriyâvâdins, of the Vainayikas, and of the Agñânavâdins;

s: philosophical systems are mastered by Mahâvîra (all)
q: he had mastered all philosophical systems, and he practised control as long as he lived.

s: Mahâvîra is omniscient omniscient
q: Omniscient, wandering about without a home, crossing the flood (of the Samsâra), wise, and of an unlimited perception, without an equal, he shines forth (or he does penance) like the sun,

s: greed is a passion (defiles the soul)
q: Having conquered the passions which defile the soul: wrath, pride, deceit, and greed,

s: Earth contains life life
q: Earth contains life, and water contains life;

s: men kill living beings (by lighting a fire)
q: He who lights a fire, kills living beings;

s: fire is killed by men (when extinguished)
q: he who extinguishes it, kills the fire.

s: wise man should not light fire (after considering the Law)
q: Therefore a wise man who well considers the Law, should light no fire.

s: plants are beings living beings (sprouts possess natural development)
q: Sprouts are beings possessed of natural development, their bodies (require) nourishment, and all have their individual life.

s: men destroy living beings (by cutting down sprouts for pleasure)
q: Reckless men who cut them down out of regard for their own pleasure, destroy many living beings.

s: men harms his own soul (by destroying seeds)
q: By destroying seeds, when young or grown up, a careless man does harm to his own soul.

s: men die death (at the expiration of their life)
q: at the expiration of their life all leave the body and die.

s: birth is difficult to obtain men (human birth)
q: If we look at the dangers (to which he is exposed) a fool has not much chance to obtain human birth;

s: Beatitude is not reached by ablutions (morning bathing)
q: Perfection is not reached by bathing in the morning, nor by abstention from acids and salt;

s: Beatitude is not obtained through water (contact with water)
q: For if perfection could be obtained by contact with water, many beings living in water must have reached perfection:

s: water contains life life
q: Earth contains life, and water contains life;

s: Beatitude is not obtained through fire (lighting fire morning and evening)
q: For if thereby perfection could be obtained, mechanics also, who use fire, would be liberated.

s: water would take off merit (if it did wash off the impure Karman)
q: If water did wash off the impure Karman, it must take off merit too.

s: wise man knows living beings (that all desire happiness)
q: A wise man, who knows the truth, should know and understand that all beings desire happiness.

s: monks abstain from violence (toward movable and immovable beings)
q: Considering this a wise monk who has ceased to sin, and guards his own self, should abstain from violence with regard to movable and (immovable) beings.

s: monks should live on water (pure water)
q: A wise man, seeing that it is sinful (to use) water, should live of pure water, till he is liberated from the Samsâra;

s: monks abstain from ablutions (as part of ascetic practice)
q: not eating seeds and bulbs, he abstains from bathing, &c., and from women.

s: monks eat for control (in order to practise control)
q: In order to be able) to practise control a monk should eat;

s: monks desire final Liberation (by getting rid of sin)
q: he should desire to get rid of sin;

s: monks should subdue passions (through control)
q: if he suffers pain, he should have recourse to control, and subdue the foe at the head of the battle, as it were.

s: living beings desire happiness (all)
q: These classes (of living beings) have been declared (by the Ginas); know and understand that they (all desire) happiness;

s: monks annihilate Karman (through endurance and control)
q: Though beaten he should be like a plank; he should wait for the advent of death; having annihilated his Karman he should not again mix with the world, but be rather like a car whose axle is broken.

s: living beings are harmed by men (through hurting them)
q: by (hurting) these beings (men) do harm to their own souls, and will again and again be born as one of them.

s: men are born as living beings (when they hurt them)
q: by (hurting) these beings (men) do harm to their own souls, and will again and again be born as one of them.

s: living beings undergo death (all, whether movable or immovable)
q: Every being born high or low in the scale of the living creation, among movable and immovable beings, will meet with its death.

s: evildoer dies for sin (sins committed in every birth)
q: Whatever sins the evildoer commits in every birth, for them he must die.

s: sinners suffer punishment (for what they inflicted on other beings)
q: In this world or in the next (the sinners suffer themselves what they have inflicted on other beings), a hundred times, or (suffer) other punishment.

s: sinners acquire Karman (while living in the Samsâra)
q: Living in the Samsâra they ever acquire new Karman, and suffer for their misdeeds.

s: Eighth Lecture, Called on Exertion is a lecture
q: Eighth Lecture, Called on Exertion.

s: living beings are targets of sciences (sciences teaching their destruction)
q: Some learn sciences which teach the destruction of living beings, others study spells for killing all sorts of creatures.

s: living beings are targets of spells (spells for killing all sorts of creatures)
q: Some learn sciences which teach the destruction of living beings, others study spells for killing all sorts of creatures.

s: deceivers pursue pleasures (through deceit)
q: Deceivers practise deceit in order to procure themselves pleasures and amusement; they kill, cut, and dismember (beings) for the sake of their own comfort.

s: sinners are subject to love and hate
q: Sinners, subject to love and hate and doing wrong, acquire Karman arising from passions and commit many sins.

s: sinners acquire Karman (arising from passions)
q: Sinners, subject to love and hate and doing wrong, acquire Karman arising from passions and commit many sins.

s: exertion has definition works (for sinners)
q: Thus the 'exertion leading to works' of the sinners has been described; now learn from me the wise men's 'exertion not leading to works.'

s: sinners commit sins (many)
q: Sinners, subject to love and hate and doing wrong, acquire Karman arising from passions and commit many sins.

s: monk is free from bonds
q: A pious monk, who is free from bonds and has severed all fetters, annihilates his bad Karman, and removes definitely the thorn (of sin).

s: monk follows right doctrine
q: Following the right doctrine he exerts himself; as one becomes more and more the receptacle of misery, so his bad thoughts (or sinfulness) increase.

s: monk annihilates Karman (bad Karman)
q: A pious monk, who is free from bonds and has severed all fetters, annihilates his bad Karman, and removes definitely the thorn (of sin).

s: monk removes thorn of sin (definitely)
q: A pious monk, who is free from bonds and has severed all fetters, annihilates his bad Karman, and removes definitely the thorn (of sin).

s: wise man conquers greed
q: Considering this, a wise man should conquer his greed, and enter upon the noble (path), which contains all virtues and is not blamed.

s: noble path contains all virtues
q: Considering this, a wise man should conquer his greed, and enter upon the noble (path), which contains all virtues and is not blamed.

s: noble path is not blamed not blamed
q: Considering this, a wise man should conquer his greed, and enter upon the noble (path), which contains all virtues and is not blamed.

s: exertion has definition abstention from works (for the virtuous)
q: Some say that it consists in works, and the pious (say that it consists) in abstention from works.

s: wise man learns religious death (when life draws towards its end)
q: When a wise man, in whatever way, comes to know that the apportioned space of his life draws towards its end, he should in the meantime quickly learn the method (of dying a religious death).

s: meditation covers sins (as a wise man's inward withdrawal)
q: As a tortoise draws its limbs into its own body, so a wise man should cover, as it were, his sins with his own meditation.

s: control requires abstention from killing
q: Do not kill living beings, do not take what is not freely given, do not talk false, treacherous speech! This is the Law of him who is rich in control.

s: Law prohibits killing living beings
q: Do not kill living beings, do not take what is not freely given, do not talk false, treacherous speech! This is the Law of him who is rich in control.

s: Law belongs to him (rich in control)
q: This is the Law of him who is rich in control.

s: the virtuous practise abstention from works
q: Some say that it consists in works, and the pious (say that it consists) in abstention from works.

s: right faith is associated with good exertion (with no evil consequences)
q: Wise men of right faith, who are renowned heroes, exert themselves in a good way which will have no (evil) consequences whatever for them.

s: austerities is not meritorious fame (when performed for fame)
q: Penance is of no good if performed by noble men who have turned monks (for the sake of fame); but that penance of which nobody else knows anything (is meritorious). Do not spread your own fame!

s: austerities is meritorious unknown to others (when nobody else knows anything about it)
q: Penance is of no good if performed by noble men who have turned monks (for the sake of fame); but that penance of which nobody else knows anything (is meritorious). Do not spread your own fame!

s: austerities should not seek fame
q: Do not spread your own fame!

s: monk practises religious practices (while meditating and abandoning the body)
q: Meditating and performing religious practices, abandoning his body, regarding forbearance as the paramount duty, a monk should wander about till he obtains liberation.

s: monk regards forbearance (as the paramount duty)
q: Meditating and performing religious practices, abandoning his body, regarding forbearance as the paramount duty, a monk should wander about till he obtains liberation.

s: monk seeks final Liberation (until obtained)
q: Meditating and performing religious practices, abandoning his body, regarding forbearance as the paramount duty, a monk should wander about till he obtains liberation.

s: final Liberation is the goal of religious practices
q: Meditating and performing religious practices, abandoning his body, regarding forbearance as the paramount duty, a monk should wander about till he obtains liberation.

s: carelessness causes Karman
q: Carelessness is called (the cause of) Karman, carefulness that of the contrary (viz. absence of Karman); when the one or the other is predicated (of a man, he is called) either a fool or a wise man.

s: carelessness is a cause (of Karman)
q: Carelessness is called (the cause of) Karman, carefulness that of the contrary (viz. absence of Karman); when the one or the other is predicated (of a man, he is called) either a fool or a wise man.

s: Karman arises from carelessness
q: Carelessness is called (the cause of) Karman, carefulness that of the contrary (viz. absence of Karman); when the one or the other is predicated (of a man, he is called) either a fool or a wise man.

s: wise man is associated with carefulness
q: Carelessness is called (the cause of) Karman, carefulness that of the contrary (viz. absence of Karman); when the one or the other is predicated (of a man, he is called) either a fool or a wise man.

s: Ninth Lecture, Called the Law is a lecture (ninth in sequence)
q: Ninth Lecture, Called the Law.

s: Kândâlas are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: Vukkasas are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: hunters are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: merchants are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: Sûdras are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: property is clung to men (by men who cling to it)
q: The iniquity of all these men who cling to property goes on increasing;

s: property is taken by pleasure-seeking relations (after acts causing death)
q: After a man has done acts which cause the death of living beings, his pleasure-seeking relations take possession of his wealth, whilst the doer of the acts must suffer for them.

s: works cause death (of living beings)
q: After a man has done acts which cause the death of living beings, his pleasure-seeking relations take possession of his wealth, whilst the doer of the acts must suffer for them.

s: works cause misery (when done to procure pleasures by sinful means)
q: for those who procure themselves pleasures by sinful acts will not get rid of misery.

s: pleasures are procured by works (when the acts are sinful)
q: for those who procure themselves pleasures by sinful acts will not get rid of misery.

s: Law is preached by Mahâvîra (as the wise Brâhmana)
q: What is the Law that has been preached by the wise Brâhmana (i.e. Mahâvîra)?

s: sin causes misery (through sinful acts)
q: for those who procure themselves pleasures by sinful acts will not get rid of misery.

s: monk is a person without property (and without egoism)
q: a monk, without property and without egoism, should follow the teaching of the Ginas.

s: monk follows Law (as the teaching of the Ginas)
q: a monk, without property and without egoism, should follow the teaching of the Ginas.

s: monk wanders worldly interests (without them)
q: (a monk) should wander about without any worldly interests.

s: monk treats tenderly living beings (in thoughts, words, and acts)
q: These six classes of living beings a wise man should know and treat tenderly, in thoughts, words, and acts;

s: monk abstains from property (when it could harm living beings)
q: he should neither do actions nor desire property whereby he might do them any harm.

s: monk abstains from untrue speech (as a cause of injury to living beings)
q: Untrue speech, sexual intercourse, personal property, taking things that are not freely given: all these causes of injury to living beings a wise man should abstain from.

s: monk abstains from sexual intercourse (as a cause of injury to living beings)
q: Untrue speech, sexual intercourse, personal property, taking things that are not freely given: all these causes of injury to living beings a wise man should abstain from.

s: monk abstains from deceit (as a cause of sin)
q: Deceit, greed, anger, and pride: combat these causes of sin; a wise man should abstain from them.

s: monk abstains from greed (as a cause of sin)
q: Deceit, greed, anger, and pride: combat these causes of sin; a wise man should abstain from them.

s: Law is noble (of the Ginas)
q: Learn from me the noble Law of the Ginas as it is.

s: monk abstains from anger (as a cause of sin)
q: Deceit, greed, anger, and pride: combat these causes of sin; a wise man should abstain from them.

s: monk abstains from pride (as a cause of sin)
q: Deceit, greed, anger, and pride: combat these causes of sin; a wise man should abstain from them.

s: monk abstains from alms (if prepared, bought, stolen, brought for him, contaminated, or unacceptable)
q: Alms that have been prepared, or bought, or stolen, or brought for the sake of a monk, or alms that contain particles of the above mentioned, or such alms as are unacceptable (for one cause or other), from all these a wise man should abstain.

s: monk abstains from speech (using as few words as possible and avoiding deception)
q: In speaking (a monk) should use as few words as possible; he should not delight in another's foibles; he should avoid deceiving speech, and should answer after ripe reflection.

s: monk avoids conduct (that is careless or associated with wicked company)
q: A virtuous monk should never keep company (with the wicked); for thereby he incurs dangers (for his conduct) disguised as pleasures.

s: monk bears pains (with a placid mind and without anger)
q: If beaten, he should not be angry; if abused, he should not fly into a passion; with a placid mind he should bear everything and not make a great noise.

s: monk obeys teachers (when they are wise and pious)
q: He should obey and serve a wise and pious teacher,

s: monk renounces worldly vanities (including excessive pride and deceit)
q: Excessive pride and deceit, all worldly vanities: all this a wise man knows and renounces, and thus brings about his final Liberation.

s: living beings include Earth (as one of six classes)
q: Earth, water, fire, and wind; grass, trees, and corn; oviparous animals, the two kinds of viviparous animals; beings engendered in fluids and in dirt, and plants;

s: living beings include water (as one of six classes)
q: Earth, water, fire, and wind; grass, trees, and corn; oviparous animals, the two kinds of viviparous animals; beings engendered in fluids and in dirt, and plants;

s: Mahâvîra is a great sage (Nirgrantha)
q: Thus spoke the Nirgrantha, the great sage Mahâvîra;

s: living beings include fire (as one of six classes)
q: Earth, water, fire, and wind; grass, trees, and corn; oviparous animals, the two kinds of viviparous animals; beings engendered in fluids and in dirt, and plants;

s: living beings include wind (as one of six classes)
q: Earth, water, fire, and wind; grass, trees, and corn; oviparous animals, the two kinds of viviparous animals; beings engendered in fluids and in dirt, and plants;

s: living beings include plants (as one of six classes)
q: Earth, water, fire, and wind; grass, trees, and corn; oviparous animals, the two kinds of viviparous animals; beings engendered in fluids and in dirt, and plants;

s: right faith is opposed by heretics (through all that they always talk about)
q: All that (the heretics) always talk about, is opposed to the right faith.

s: final Liberation is brought about by monk (through renunciation of worldly vanities)
q: Excessive pride and deceit, all worldly vanities: all this a wise man knows and renounces, and thus brings about his final Liberation.

s: Mahâvîra possesses infinite knowledge and faith
q: he who possesses infinite knowledge and faith has taught the Law and the sacred texts.

s: Mahâvîra teaches sacred texts (as one possessing infinite knowledge and faith)
q: he who possesses infinite knowledge and faith has taught the Law and the sacred texts.

s: Brâhmanas are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: Kshattriyas are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: Vaisyas are accustomed to do works (as one of the listed social groups)
q: Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaisyas, Kândâlas, Vukkasas, hunters, merchants, Sûdras, and others who are accustomed to do acts;

s: Tenth Lecture, Called Carefulness is a lecture
q: Tenth Lecture, Called Carefulness.

s: monk uses allowed food (as his sustenance)
q: Having mastered the Law and got rid of carelessness, he should live on allowed food, and treat all beings as he himself would be treated; he should not expose himself to guilt by his desire for life; a monk who performs austerities should not keep any store. (3)

s: monk avoids unallowed food (as a matter of conduct)
q: He should not desire unallowed food, and he should not mix with people who desire such; he should mortify his flesh, thinking (of his duty), and giving up his sorrows without regard (to worldly interests). (11)

s: monk restrains from women (sexual intercourse)
q: Abstain from sexual intercourse with women, do not acquire property; a man possessed of carefulness will, beyond doubt, be a saviour (to others) in all circumstances. (13)

s: living beings suffer misery (and are afflicted)
q: Restraining his senses from women, a sage should wander about free from all worldly ties. See, every creature and every being suffers pain and is afflicted. (4)

s: monk does not injure living beings (through carefulness)
q: He should not expose himself to guilt by his desire for life, but he should wander about without any attachment. Speaking after due consideration, and combating his worldly desires, he should say nothing that involves slaughter of living beings. (10)

s: sin is committed by injuring living beings
q: Doing harm to these beings, an ignorant man becomes involved in sins. Sin is committed by injuring (beings), and one sins also by employing others (in such acts). (5)

s: sin increases Karman (through violent deeds)
q: Given to violent deeds he accumulates (Karman); on his decease he (meets with) really distressing misery. Therefore a wise man considers well the Law; a sage wanders about free from all worldly ties. (9)

s: Karman is accumulated by monk (through violent deeds)
q: Given to violent deeds he accumulates (Karman); on his decease he (meets with) really distressing misery.

s: sin causes misery (on decease)
q: Given to violent deeds he accumulates (Karman); on his decease he (meets with) really distressing misery.

s: Tenth Lecture, Called Carefulness is called carefulness
q: Tenth Lecture, Called Carefulness.

s: Ginas enjoin carefulness (thorough)
q: He too who leads a miserable life, commits sin. Therefore (the Ginas) have enjoined thorough carefulness.

s: control is delighted in monk (with sound judgment)
q: One should know the truth, delight in control and sound judgment, cease from injuring beings, and be of a settled mind. (6)

s: monk delights in control (with sound judgment)
q: One should know the truth, delight in control and sound judgment, cease from injuring beings, and be of a settled mind. (6)

s: monk avoids honour and fame (as worldly attachments)
q: A pious monk, free from bonds, should wander about desiring neither honours nor fame. (23)

s: monk does not acquire property
q: Abstain from sexual intercourse with women, do not acquire property; a man possessed of carefulness will, beyond doubt, be a saviour (to others) in all circumstances. (13)

s: final Liberation is obtained by monk (through realizing singleness and solitude)
q: Try to realise that you are single and alone; thereby you will obtain Liberation; mind, this is no false assertion! This Liberation is not anything unreal, but the best thing.

s: final Liberation is best thing (not unreal)
q: This Liberation is not anything unreal, but the best thing.

s: monk conquers sensual objects (through control)
q: A monk having conquered aversion to control and delight in sensual objects, should bear all troubles caused by (pricking) grass, cold, heat, and insects; he should endure pleasant and unpleasant smells. (14)

s: monk endures troubles (caused by grass, cold, heat, and insects)
q: A monk having conquered aversion to control and delight in sensual objects, should bear all troubles caused by (pricking) grass, cold, heat, and insects; he should endure pleasant and unpleasant smells. (14)

s: Arhat is a wise
q: The wise (Arhat) having pondered on the Law proclaimed it; learn from me correctly what is carefulness.

s: monk guards speech (with carefulness)
q: Guarding his speech and possessed of carefulness, acquiring (pure) Lêsyâ, he should wander about; he should not thatch a house for himself or for others, nor behave towards other people like a householder. (15)

s: monk acquires Lêsyâ (pure)
q: Guarding his speech and possessed of carefulness, acquiring (pure) Lêsyâ, he should wander about; he should not thatch a house for himself or for others, nor behave towards other people like a householder. (15)

s: monk does not build house (for himself or others)
q: Guarding his speech and possessed of carefulness, acquiring (pure) Lêsyâ, he should wander about; he should not thatch a house for himself or for others, nor behave towards other people like a householder. (15)

s: absolute (âtman) is maintained as unchangeable character (by somebody)
q: Questioned by somebody who maintains the unchangeable character of the soul, he should expound the true (doctrine); those who engage in works and are held in worldly bondage, do not know the Law which leads to Liberation. (16)

s: works cause worldly bondage (for those who engage in them)
q: those who engage in works and are held in worldly bondage, do not know the Law which leads to Liberation. (16)

s: Law leads to final Liberation
q: those who engage in works and are held in worldly bondage, do not know the Law which leads to Liberation. (16)

s: Kriyâvâdins adhere to doctrine (among various opinions)
q: Men here have various opinions; (they adhere) to the doctrine of the Kriyâvâdins and Akriyâvâdins.

s: Akriyâvâdins adhere to doctrine (among various opinions)
q: Men here have various opinions; (they adhere) to the doctrine of the Kriyâvâdins and Akriyâvâdins.

s: Arhat proclaims Law
q: The wise (Arhat) having pondered on the Law proclaimed it; learn from me correctly what is carefulness.

s: monk does not speak untruth (when setting out for Liberation)
q: A sage setting out for the real good (viz. Liberation), should not speak untruth; this (rule, they say,) comprises Nirvâna and the whole of carefulness

s: untruth is excluded by carefulness (as part of the rule comprising Nirvâna)
q: A sage setting out for the real good (viz. Liberation), should not speak untruth; this (rule, they say,) comprises Nirvâna and the whole of carefulness

s: Nirvâna is comprised by carefulness (together with the rule against untruth)
q: A sage setting out for the real good (viz. Liberation), should not speak untruth; this (rule, they say,) comprises Nirvâna and the whole of carefulness

s: monk does not desire life (as one who has gone beyond the Circle of Births)
q: A monk who has left the house and is free from desires should abandon his body, annihilating his sins; he should not desire life nor death, and walk about, having got beyond the Circle (of Births). (24)

s: monk does not desire death (as one who has gone beyond the Circle of Births)
q: A monk who has left the house and is free from desires should abandon his body, annihilating his sins; he should not desire life nor death, and walk about, having got beyond the Circle (of Births). (24)

s: Law is pondered on by Arhat
q: The wise (Arhat) having pondered on the Law proclaimed it; learn from me correctly what is carefulness.

s: carefulness is taught monk (as the proper mode of wandering)
q: A monk who forms no resolutions and is possessed of carefulness, should wander about, giving no offence to any creature; (1)

s: monk is a ascetic
q: A monk who has left the house and is free from desires should abandon his body, annihilating his sins; he should not desire life nor death, and walk about, having got beyond the Circle (of Births). (24)

s: monk possesses carefulness
q: A monk who forms no resolutions and is possessed of carefulness, should wander about, giving no offence to any creature; (1)

q: Uttaradhyayana Sutra (Uttarâdhyayana Sûtra), Lectures 1-18, translated by Hermann Jacobi First Lecture.

s: ill-behaved pupil is insubordinate to teacher (and inattentive)
q: But a monk who, on receiving an order from his superior, does not walk up to him, being insubordinate and inattentive, is called ill-behaved.

s: teacher blames evil acts
q: The teacher's) instruction, his manner of giving it, and his blaming evil acts are considered blissful by the intelligent, but hateful by the bad monk.

s: pupil learns sacred text (according to tradition)
q: When a pupil who observes the above rules of conduct, questions the teacher about the sacred text, its meaning, or both, he should deliver it according to tradition.

s: virtue is preferred to evil ways
q: As a pig leaves a trough filled with grain to feed on faeces, so a brute (of a man) turns away from virtue, and takes to evil ways.

s: good conduct supports welfare (one's own)
q: Hearing a man thus compared to a dog and a pig, he who desires his own welfare, should adhere to good conduct.

s: righteousness is acquired through discipline
q: Therefore be eager for discipline, that you may acquire righteousness; a son of the wise, who desires liberation, will not be turned away from anywhere.

s: liberation is desired by pupil (a son of the wise)
q: Therefore be eager for discipline, that you may acquire righteousness; a son of the wise, who desires liberation, will not be turned away from anywhere.

s: wise people value instruction (including rough instruction)
q: Wise, fearless monks consider even a rough instruction as a benefit, but the fools hate it, though it produces patience and purity of mind.

s: wise people practices the conduct (attained by their virtues)
q: He who adopts the conduct which the wise ones have attained by their virtues and always practised, will not incur blame.

s: Self is difficult to subdue subdue
q: Subdue your Self, for the Self is difficult to subdue; if your Self is subdued, you will be happy in this world and in the next.

q: A monk should avoid untruth, nor should he speak positively (about future things, his plans, &c.); he should avoid sinful speech, and always keep free from deceit.

q: His knowledge will be honoured, his doubts will be removed, he will gladden the heart of his teacher by his good acts; kept in safety by the performance of austerities and by meditation, being as it were a great light, he will keep the five vows.

s: monk may become Siddha (on leaving the body; eternal)
q: Honoured by gods, Gandharvas, and men, he will, on leaving this body which consists of dirt and impurities, become either an eternal Siddha, or a god of great power and small imperfections.

s: discipline is a virtue (when influenced by eight causes)
q: For eight causes discipline is called virtue, viz.: not to be fond of mirth, to control one's self, not to speak evil of others, not to be without discipline, not to be of wrong discipline, not to be covetous, not to be choleric, to love the truth; for their influence discipline is called virtue.

q: He who always acknowledges his allegiance to his teacher, who has religious zeal and ardour for study, who is kind in words and actions, deserves to be instructed.

s: monk has piety (when very learned)

q: There are five causes which render wholesome discipline impossible: egoism, delusion, carelessness, illness, and idleness:

s: monk is superior to other monks (when very learned)
q: As a trained Kambôga-steed, whom no noise frightens, exceeds all other horses in speed, so a very learned monk is superior to all others.

s: monk equals hero (when very learned)
q: As a valiant hero bestriding a trained horse, with heralds singing out to his right and left, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals elephant (when very learned)
q: As a strong and irresistible elephant of sixty years, surrounded by his females, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals bullock (when very learned)
q: As a sharp-horned, strong-necked bullock, the leader of the herd, is a fine sight, so is a very learned monk.

s: monk is superior to animals (when very learned, like a proud lion)
q: As a proud lion with sharp fangs, who brooks no assault, is superior to all animals, so is a very learned monk (superior to all men).

s: monk equals Vâsudêva (when very learned)
q: As Vâsudêva, the god with the conch, discus, and club, who fights with an irresistible strength, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals universal monarch (when very learned)
q: As a universal monarch with his fourfold army and great power, the possessor of the fourteen attributes of a king, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals Sakra (when very learned)
q: As Sakra the thousand-eyed, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the fortress-destroyer, the king of gods, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals sun (when very learned)
q: As the rising sun, the dispeller of darkness, who burns as it were with light, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals moon (when very learned)
q: As the moon, the queen of the stars, surrounded by the asterisms, when she is full at full-moon, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals storehouse (when very learned)
q: As a well-guarded storehouse of merchants, which is filled with grain of many kinds, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals Gambû tree (when very learned)
q: As the best of Gambû trees, called Sudarsanâ, which is the abode of the presiding deity, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals Sîtâ (when very learned)
q: As the best of rivers, the ocean-flowing stream Sîtâ with its dark waters, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals Mandara (when very learned)
q: As the best of hills, high mount Mandara, on which various plants shed a bright lustre, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk equals ocean (when very learned)
q: As the ocean of inexhaustible water, the delight of Svayambhû, which is full of precious things of many kinds, (has no equal), neither has a very learned monk.

s: monk is deep ocean (when monks equal the ocean in depth)
q: Monks who equal the ocean in depth, who are difficult to overcome, are frightened by nobody (or nothing), and are not easily assailed, who are full of extensive learning and take care of themselves, will go to the highest place, after their Karman has been annihilated.

s: Harikêsa-Bala is a monk (chaste and self-controlled)
q: Harikêsa-Bala was born in a family of Svapâkas (Kândâlas); he became a monk and a sage, possessed of the highest virtues, who had subdued his senses.

q: The noble (monk) said 'yes,' and took food and drink after having fasted a whole month.

s: Harikêsa-Bala is that austere ascetic (of noble nature)
q: He is that austere ascetic, of noble nature, who subdues his senses and controls himself; the chaste man, who would not accept me when my own father, king Kausalika, gave me to him.

s: Brâhmanas is a blessed fields (when of pure birth and knowledge)
q: All the world knows that we are (as it were) the field on which gifts sown grow up as merit; Brâhmanas of pure birth and knowledge are the blessed fields.

s: Brâhmanas tends fire (through sacrificial practice)
q: O Brâhmanas, why do you tend the fire, and seek external purity by water?

s: Brahmanical sacrifice is a sacrifice (Brahmanical)

s: Yaksha of the Tinduka-tree protects Harikêsa-Bala (by assisting him against his attackers)
q: When the Yakshas heard these well-spoken words of (the Purôhita's) wife Bhadrâ, they came to the assistance of the sage, and kept the young men off.

s: Bhadrâ is a daughter (of king Kausalika)
q: At that turn king Kausalika's daughter, Bhadrâ, of faultless body, saw that the monk was beaten, and appeased the angry youngsters.

q: He is the very man to whom the king, impelled by the devil (who possessed me), had given me, but who would not think of me; he is the sage whom princes and gods adore, who has refused me.

s: young men assault Harikêsa-Bala (with sticks, canes, and whips)
q: On these words of the teachers, many young fellows rushed forward, and they all beat the sage with sticks, canes, and whips.

s: Asuras beats the people (appearing in the air with hideous shapes)

s: gods praise Harikêsa-Bala (for the power of his penance)
q: 'The value of penance has become visible, birth appears of no value! Look at the holy Harikêsa, the son of a Svapâka, whose power is so great.'
